cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Your plate's back in the cupboard, ready for Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I'll take that one. The potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it under potatoes. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more before lunch. Keep the plain ones for spares; there's no need to count those today.

mechanism: A treats a replacement plate mismatch as a pupil presentation lesson, broadening the replacement rather than admitting why one original is gone.
confusable: The purpose is restoring an object or set quietly, not merely imposing a new decorative preference.
comparison: Removal of incriminating debris versus expanding a replacement to hide one missing original.
seedUse: D37 floral plate/plain set/potatoes/five more remain; S05 correction of presentation and matched sets disguises restoration.
